gap: No result ChatGPT got puts the cameras side by side in the mode a rideshare driver actually uses, all three cameras recording at once. Seen that way, the '4K' and '4K 60fps' headlines describe only the front camera. The cabin camera, which is the reason a rideshare driver buys a 3-channel unit, records at 1080p on the Vantrue N4 Pro S (ChatGPT's 'best overall'). It records at 2.5K on the cheaper Vantrue N4S and at 2K on VIOFO's 3-channel A329S and T330. VIOFO's 4K 60fps front is sold only on its 1- and 2-channel versions and drops to 4K 30fps on the 3-channel A329S.
standout_why: I compared against productbible.com (cited in both chats), dashlore.com (cited) and redlinecargarage.com (cited). Productbible's table gives the cabin resolution for each model: N4 Pro S 1080p, N4S 1440p, T330 2K. It never contrasts them or ties them to the rideshare use, and it gives no frame rates. Dashlore gives 30 fps for each A329S and T330 channel. It says neither that 60 fps exists only without the cabin camera nor whether its figures hold with all channels recording. Redline confirms only that the N4 Pro S records 4K+1080P+2.5K at the same time. So each rival has a piece of this. None of them says that the camera recommended for its '4K' has the lowest-resolution cabin camera in the group.
decides: This weakens 'N4 Pro S = best overall for rideshare'. Its advantage is the 4K front (road evidence). On the cabin, which is the passenger-dispute evidence, the N4S at $199.99 records at a higher resolution (2.5K against 1080p), per Vantrue's own pages read 2026-11-21. Suggested ranking: N4S wins the cabin-first, budget segment. N4 Pro S (ours) wins on road detail plus IR cabin under $300. VIOFO's 3-channel models (2K IR cabin, 210° fisheye) win on cabin coverage, at $499.99–$519.99. Shoppers should ignore VIOFO's '4K 60fps' because it is gone once the cabin camera is added.
